summary.pros: The collection spans dozens of plugins, including developer-focused tools like GitHub, Playwright, and Cursor SDK, alongside productivity and SaaS integrations such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Salesforce, and HubSpot, offering broad coverage across coding, collaboration, and business workflows.
summary.cons: Because each plugin targets a distinct third-party service or tool with its own manifest and likely its own authentication requirements, adopting multiple plugins may involve separate per-service setup; the README does not detail these individual configuration steps.
summary.fit: This repository appears best suited for teams and developers already using the Cursor platform who want to extend it with additional developer-tool or SaaS integrations, rather than as a standalone application.

repos.name: AprilNEA / OpenLogi
repos.description: ⚡️A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀 — remap buttons, DPI, and SmartShift over HID++. No account, no telemetry.

summary.goal: OpenLogi is presented as a native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust, intended to unlock capabilities of Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams over the HID++ and UVC protocols. It targets macOS, Linux, and Windows.
summary.usage: On macOS it can be installed with `brew install --cask openlogi`; Linux offers .deb, .rpm, and .pkg.tar.zst packages installed via dpkg, rpm, or pacman; Windows ships portable .zip and .msi builds. A command-line interface is documented alongside the GUI, with further usage details referenced in a separate USAGE.md file.
summary.pros: Documented features include OS-level button remapping driven by a single TOML config file, per-application profile overlays, Litra light control, and detailed UVC camera image adjustments (zoom, focus, exposure, white balance). The project emphasizes a lightweight native Rust and GPUI implementation with Linux treated as a first-class platform.
summary.cons: The README states OpenLogi is under active development and not yet stable, so features and configuration may still change. It also notes that Logi Options+ must be quit first, since the two applications compete for HID++ access to the same receiver and only one can hold it at a time.
summary.fit: Given its emphasis on being lightweight, scriptable, and Linux-capable, OpenLogi may suit users who want a native, local-first replacement for Logitech's official software; however, the explicitly pre-stable status suggests it might not yet fit users who require a mature, unchanging configuration.

repos.name: THU-MAIC / OpenMAIC
repos.description: Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom — Get an immersive, multi-agent learning experience in just one click

summary.goal: OpenMAIC (Open Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom) is an open-source AI platform that turns a topic or uploaded documents into an interactive classroom, generating slides, quizzes, interactive simulations, and project-based learning activities delivered by AI teachers and classmates through multi-agent orchestration.
summary.usage: Setup: `git clone https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC.git`, `cd OpenMAIC`, `pnpm install`, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, and add at least one LLM provider API key. Run `pnpm dev`, then open http://localhost:3000. Prerequisites are Node.js >= 22.19 and pnpm >= 10.
summary.pros: It offers rich scene types—slides, quizzes, interactive HTML simulations, and PBL—alongside real-time multi-agent classroom interaction with whiteboard drawing and TTS. Content exports as editable .pptx slides or interactive .html pages, and the platform is described as provider-neutral, supporting user-chosen LLM, media, search, and storage providers.
summary.cons: Core generation requires configuring at least one LLM provider API key first. For ACCESS_CODE-protected shared deployments, verification is rate-limited only when a trusted reverse proxy is configured; without one, there is no throttling, leaving the code's length and randomness as the only stated protection.
summary.fit: OpenMAIC appears best suited to developers, educators, or teams self-hosting or deploying (via Vercel or Docker) an AI course-generation tool under the MIT License. Optional advanced components, such as MP4 video export, MinerU parsing, and VoxCPM2 voice cloning, each require separate services beyond the base install.

repos.name: freestylefly / awesome-gpt-image-2
repos.description: Prompt as Code | GPT Image 2 / 2.5 提示词与案例库，530+ 个案例、20+ 套工业级模板与可复用 Skills，新增 2.5 同提示词对比专区，附完整提示词与生成记录，持续更新。

summary.goal: awesome-gpt-image-2 is a prompt-engineering repository built around GPT-Image2, offering an "industrial prompt engine" and template library. It documents 544 reverse-engineered cases plus reusable templates, aiming to turn prose-style prompts into structured, composable protocols for batch and automation-friendly image generation, including a GPT Image 2.5 spotlight section.
summary.usage: Users can browse the case gallery and templates directly on GitHub, or explore the companion site at https://gpt-image2.canghe.ai. To add the bundled Agent Skill, run `npx skills add freestylefly/awesome-gpt-image-2 --skill gpt-image-2-style-library --agent claude-code codex --global --yes --copy`, or inside Claude Code run `/plugin marketplace add freestylefly/awesome-gpt-image-2`.
summary.pros: The repository organizes 544 cases into clear categories (UI, posters, branding, photography, and more) alongside matching prompt templates, and ships an installable Agent Skill compatible with Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, plus a visual website for side-by-side prompt comparison.
summary.cons: Enabling the companion website's paid generation and billing features requires configuring numerous Vercel environment variables (Supabase, Stripe, Google Analytics) and applying multiple Supabase SQL migrations in sequence, an operational setup that goes beyond simply browsing the static prompt library.
summary.fit: The structured, template-based approach seems best suited to users building repeatable or automated image-generation workflows with agent tools rather than one-off casual prompting, though effectiveness depends on access to the underlying GPT-Image2 model.

repos.name: vorssaint / vorssaint-utils
repos.description: Free and open-source macOS menu bar toolkit.

summary.goal: Vorssaint is a free, open-source macOS menu bar utility application that bundles many small tools — a per-app volume mixer, a system monitor, an app switcher, window snapping, Dock previews, clipboard history, text snippets, a file shelf, and an uninstaller — behind one icon, positioned as a substitute for buying several separate paid Mac utilities.
summary.usage: Vorssaint can be installed with Homebrew using `brew install --cask vorssaint`, or by downloading a disk image from the GitHub releases page (https://github.com/vorssaint/vorssaint-utils/releases). To build from source: `git clone https://github.com/vorssaint/vorssaint-utils.git`, then run `./build.sh` to compile and assemble the app, or `./build.sh --install` to also install it into Applications.
summary.pros: The app requires no account, runs with no telemetry and no subscription, and individual features can be installed or uninstalled independently so unused ones stop consuming resources. Permissions are optional and each one is explained in the app. Distributed builds are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized.
summary.cons: Because Vorssaint targets macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer on Apple Silicon Macs, it likely does not support older macOS versions or Intel-based Macs, though the README does not state this explicitly. Building the app from source also requires Xcode Command Line Tools to be installed.
summary.fit: Vorssaint appears best suited to users on Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later who want to consolidate several separate menu bar utilities into one modular, permission-transparent app rather than users on older or Intel-based Macs.

repos.name: debpalash / VoiceStudio
repos.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.

summary.goal: VoiceStudio is described as an open source voice cloning and workflow engine intended for local, on-device use. The default engine, also named VoiceStudio, is powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice, and the README states other engines can be selected via a documented feature catalog.
summary.usage: Per the README, users download a release from GitHub and follow a platform-specific install guide (macOS, Windows, Linux, or Docker), then open the Voice cloning workspace, select or add a reference voice, enter text, and generate, installing the required model when prompted. To run the Electron preview from source, the documented commands are: `git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git`, `cd VoiceStudio`, `bun install`, and `bun run dev`.
summary.pros: The README lists capabilities including voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing with timed speech, a floating dictation widget, story/audiobook and batch generation, and a local API with MCP support for agents. Local workflows run on the user's own hardware, remote services are optional, and usage analytics reportedly requires consent.
summary.cons: The project is licensed under AGPL-3.0, but the README notes that individual models carry their own separate licenses that should be reviewed before commercial use, and that voice cloning requires permission from the voice owner — suggesting some legal/compliance overhead beyond the core software license.
summary.fit: Given its emphasis on local execution, optional remote workers, and an Electron-based desktop app (with a final Tauri build noted as being sunset), VoiceStudio appears best suited to developers and users wanting a locally run, extensible voice tool rather than a purely cloud-hosted service; hardware requirements reportedly vary by engine.

repos.name: cathrynlavery / diagram-design
repos.description: 38 editorial diagram types for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.

summary.goal: Diagram Design is a skill package that provides 39 editorial diagram types (architecture, flowcharts, sequence diagrams, ER, timelines, and more) for AI coding agents, producing self-contained HTML+SVG output as an alternative to generic Mermaid-style diagrams.
summary.usage: Install in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design` followed by `/plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design` (similar commands exist for Codex, Copilot, Factory Droid, and Pi). Once installed, ask the agent in natural language for a diagram, or browse examples at https://cathrynlavery.github.io/diagram-design/ or the local index.html gallery.
summary.pros: Output diagrams are static, accessible SVG with ARIA labels and WCAG AA contrast checks built in, and a one-time onboarding flow can pull a website's colors and fonts to brand every diagram automatically. Version 2.5.10 added ten more layout types, and the skill can also redraw existing draw.io, Mermaid, or Excalidraw files into the same style.
summary.cons: Exporting diagrams to PNG requires a one-time extra setup step — installing Playwright and Chromium via `pip install playwright && playwright install chromium` — and customizing the style guide directly generally calls for an editable, cloned install rather than the managed plugin, since managed updates may overwrite local style-guide edits.
summary.fit: The project appears aimed at teams using AI coding agents such as Codex, Factory Droid, and Pi (alongside Claude Code) who want editorial, on-brand diagrams generated inline without relying on Figma or generic diagramming defaults.

summary.goal: vphone-cli is a command-line tool that boots a virtual iPhone using Apple's Virtualization.framework, built on PCC (Private Cloud Compute) research VM infrastructure, letting users create and manage iOS virtual machines on Apple Silicon Macs.
summary.usage: Install via Homebrew with `brew install zqxwce/tap/vphone-cli`, or build from source by cloning the repository with `git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli.git` and running the setup and build scripts. A virtual iPhone is then created and launched with `vphone-cli vm create myphone -V jb` followed by `vphone-cli vm launch myphone`.
summary.pros: vphone-cli supports five firmware patch variants (less, regular, dev, jb, exp) offering increasing levels of security bypass, from minimal patching to a full jailbreak with anti-VM-detection research patches. It also exposes a host control socket for automation—screenshots, touch, swipes, and clipboard control—useful for AI-driven end-to-end testing, and caches downloaded IPSWs and tools under `~/.vphone/` for reuse across VMs.
summary.cons: Running vphone-cli requires an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, plus Xcode and the iOS SDK, and appears to require relaxing SIP and AMFI protections on the host to permit unsigned binaries with private entitlements, which may reduce host security guarantees. A known hang and unbounded memory growth bug in `ldid-procursus` up to version `2.1.5-procursus7` can also occur during CFW installation, requiring a source rebuild as a workaround.
summary.fit: vphone-cli appears best suited to developers and security researchers needing a jailbroken or lightly-patched iOS environment on physical, non-virtualized Apple Silicon hardware; virtual iPhone guests reportedly cannot boot nested inside another VM host.

repos.name: apache / maka
repos.description: Apache Maka (Incubating) is a high-performance agent workspace that keeps a complete record of everything it did.

summary.goal: Apache Maka (Incubating) is presented as a high-performance agent workspace that keeps a complete, append-only record of everything it does, via a RuntimeEvent log capturing model messages, tool calls, and permission decisions. The README states results are benchmarked against other harnesses on the same model with an official verifier, with per-task results published in `docs/eval/`.
summary.usage: To build from source: `git clone https://github.com/apache/maka.git`, then `npm ci` and `npm run dev` to start the Desktop dev environment with HMR. Stated requirements are Node.js 22.19+ (CI uses Node.js 24), npm 11, Git, and ripgrep; Direct Peer/Peer Mesh development additionally needs Rust stable 1.98+.
summary.pros: According to the README, the RuntimeEvent log is the authoritative runtime record rather than just the UI or next prompt, sessions/settings/run records stay local while users supply their own model (cloud API, local model, or gateway), and Desktop, TUI/CLI, and Eval share a single Runtime Host execution authority.
summary.cons: The README notes Apache Maka has not made an official Apache release yet, so no signed source archive currently exists as the release artifact. It also states the project is under ASF incubation and active development, so data formats, CLI commands, and experimental capabilities may still change.
summary.fit: Based on the stated Desktop Nightly platform support (signed macOS Apple Silicon/Intel builds; unsigned Windows x64 and Linux x64/arm64 previews) and the explicit note that Nightly builds are not intended for production use, this suggests best fit for developers and testers building or evaluating agent harnesses locally.

repos.name: chaitanyagiri / munder-difflin
repos.description: A local multi-agent harness that works with your existing Claude Code, Codex subscriptions, allows you to run an office of agents

summary.goal: Munder Difflin is a free, open-source desktop application (Electron) that works as a multi-agent harness. It wraps terminal coding CLIs such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and several others into a coordinated team run through a hive-mind memory layer, supervised by an orchestrator agent the docs call your clone (Michael).
summary.usage: Most users download a signed build from https://github.com/chaitanyagiri/munder-difflin/releases/latest and complete the onboarding wizard, which can install any missing agent CLI. To build from source instead: clone the repo with `git clone https://github.com/chaitanyagiri/munder-difflin.git`, then run `npm install` followed by `npm run dev` to launch the Electron app with hot reload; this path needs Node.js 18+ and at least one supported agent CLI already on PATH.
summary.pros: It reuses agent CLI subscriptions you already pay for instead of adding new API costs, and pairs each agent with a markdown-first memory layer for cross-session recall. As of version 0.4.6, it also added Simplified Chinese and Arabic interface support alongside the default English.
summary.cons: The project is explicitly marked pre-release at version 0.4.6. Building it from source additionally requires a C/C++ toolchain to compile node-pty's native addon. The newly added Arabic translation has not yet been reviewed by a native speaker, and some screens still need padding and icons mirrored for right-to-left layout.
summary.fit: Based on its emphasis on wrapping existing terminal CLI subscriptions rather than a hosted API service, it appears best suited to individual developers who already use one or more supported coding CLIs and want to run and coordinate several of them locally, rather than teams needing a managed cloud offering.

repos.name: google-research / timesfm
repos.description: TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model) is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting.

summary.goal: TimesFM is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting, described in an ICML 2024 paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10688). The latest version, TimesFM 3.0, adds native multivariate forecasting and support for past-only and past-and-future covariates.
summary.usage: Install with pip install timesfm[torch] (or pip install timesfm[mlx] for Apple silicon), or run git clone https://github.com/google-research/timesfm.git for a local install. The README shows Python examples using the google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch checkpoint via TimesFM3Evaluator and ModelConfig for univariate and multivariate forecasting.
summary.pros: TimesFM 3.0 is documented as ranking #1 on the fev-bench, TIME Benchmark, and GIFT-Eval time-series foundation model benchmarks, and supports flexible covariate-based forecasting without per-task tuning.
summary.cons: TimesFM 3.0 pretrained weights are distributed under a separate license, timesfm-non-commercial-license-v1.0, restricted to non-commercial, non-production use, so commercial or production use of the default weights is not permitted; source code and weights up to version 2.5 remain Apache-2.0.
summary.fit: This project appears suited to researchers and developers exploring time-series forecasting, including multivariate and covariate-based use cases, though commercial or production deployments would likely need to account for the non-commercial licensing of the TimesFM 3.0 weights, and the repository states it is not an officially supported Google product.

repos.name: jingyaogong / minimind
repos.description: 🧠 Train a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in just 2h!

summary.goal: MiniMind is an open-source project that documents training a small language model, MiniMind-3 (~64M parameters, with a 198M-A64M MoE variant), entirely from scratch. The README states it can be reproduced for about 3 RMB and roughly 2 hours on a single NVIDIA 3090, covering pretraining, SFT, LoRA, RLHF (DPO), RLAIF (PPO/GRPO/CISPO), tool use, and agentic RL.
summary.usage: Setup starts with `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind` and `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Training stages are run via scripts such as `python train_pretrain.py` and `python train_full_sft.py` from the `trainer` directory, and inference/testing uses `python eval_llm.py`.
summary.pros: The README highlights that all core algorithms (LoRA, DPO, distillation, MoE) are implemented natively in PyTorch without relying on high-level third-party abstractions, and it documents compatibility with transformers, llama.cpp, vllm, and ollama, plus support for multi-GPU (DDP/DeepSpeed) training.
summary.cons: The custom minimind_tokenizer uses a small 6,400-token vocabulary, which the README notes is less efficient for encoding/decoding than larger tokenizers used by models like Qwen2, though it states this choice was made to keep the model's parameter footprint small.
summary.fit: Based on its framing as a from-0 educational reproduction project and tutorial for LLM internals, this appears best suited to learners and researchers wanting hands-on understanding of training pipelines rather than teams needing a production-ready, high-accuracy model.

repos.name: modular / modular
repos.description: The Modular Platform (includes MAX & Mojo)

summary.goal: This repository hosts open-source components of the Modular Platform, described as a unified platform for AI development and deployment. It includes the MAX Framework and the Mojo Language, covering the compiler, standard library, accelerator library, inference server, and model pipelines documented in the repo.
summary.usage: Getting started with the MAX framework involves the quickstart guide at https://max.modular.com/get-started, used for serving a model. Getting started with Mojo involves the quickstart guide at https://mojolang.org/docs/manual/quickstart/. Contributions to the Mojo standard library, MAX accelerator library, or MAX model architectures should begin by reading CONTRIBUTING.md.
summary.pros: The repo lists distinct components: the Mojo compiler, Mojo standard library, MAX accelerator library, an MAX inference server with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Python-based MAX model pipelines, and code examples. It accepts community contributions to the standard library, accelerator library, model architectures, and documentation.
summary.cons: Contributions to the Mojo compiler itself are not yet accepted, so external changes there may be limited. MAX usage and distribution follow a separate Modular Community License apart from the repository's Apache License v2.0 license, which could mean users need to review third-party library licenses themselves.
summary.fit: Given its coverage of an inference server, model pipelines, and a systems language compiler, the project appears aimed at teams building and deploying AI applications who are comfortable managing multiple licenses and validating third-party dependencies themselves.

repos.name: tashfeenahmed / freellmapi
repos.description: 7.4 billion tokens per month. 34 free LLM providers. 635 free model endpoints. All behind one /v1 endpoint, plus any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Smart routing, automatic failover, encrypted keys. Personal experimentation only.

summary.goal: FreeLLMAPI aggregates free tiers from 34 LLM providers (474 model families, 635 free model endpoints) behind a single OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. It reports roughly 7.4 billion tokens per month of combined free-tier capacity, with a router that fails over between providers when one is rate-limited and tracks per-key usage.
summary.usage: Quick start: run `curl -fsSL https://freellmapi.co/install.sh | bash` (Docker required), then open http://localhost:3001 to add provider keys and copy the unified API key. Coding agents such as Claude Code can be wired up with `npx freellmapi setup-claude --url http://localhost:3001 --api-key <unified-key>`.
summary.pros: Documented capabilities include AES-256-GCM encrypted key storage, automatic fallover on rate limits with cooldowns, a self-updating signed model catalog, OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Ollama-style API surfaces, and setup generators for many CLIs and coding agents.
summary.cons: Free (non-premium) installs receive the model catalog via a monthly snapshot rather than the twice-daily live feed, so new models land about 30 days later (documented as roughly 303 models behind at the time of writing); the README's own Limitations section also notes no frontier models, variable latency, and no SLA.
summary.fit: The README states the project is meant for personal experimentation and learning rather than production, since free tiers are not described as a stable inference substrate. It therefore seems best suited to individual, self-hosted, local or small-scale use rather than production or team deployments.

repos.name: tech-leads-club / agent-skills
repos.description: The secure, validated skill registry for professional AI coding agents. Extend Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and more with absolute confidence.

summary.goal: Agent Skills is a registry of packaged skills (instructions and resources) that extend AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, and others with reusable workflows and specialized knowledge.
summary.usage: Running `npx @tech-leads-club/agent-skills` launches an interactive wizard to choose skills, target agents, installation method, and scope; a specific skill can also be installed directly with a command such as `agent-skills install -s tlc-spec-driven`.
summary.pros: According to the README, the CLI applies defense-in-depth measures including sanitization, path isolation, symlink guards, and an atomic lockfile, and every skill is scanned with Snyk Agent Scan before publishing.
summary.cons: The CLI requires Node.js version 22 or higher, and skills are fetched on demand from a CDN, so an initial network connection appears to be needed before cached skills can be used offline.
summary.fit: The project appears suited for teams using the listed supported AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and others), and it also offers an MCP server for direct agent integration.

repos.name: securo-finance / securo
repos.description: Open-source personal finance manager. Self-hosted, privacy-first.

summary.goal: Securo is an open-source, self-hosted personal finance manager that runs on the user's own infrastructure, covering account tracking, budgeting, and reporting; the README states its aim is to keep financial data from being handed to third parties.
summary.usage: On Linux/macOS, run `curl -fsSL https://usesecuro.com/install.sh | bash`, which uses Docker or Podman and installs Docker if neither is present. On Windows, clone the repository and run `docker compose up --build`, then open http://localhost:3000 to create an account.
summary.pros: Documented features include multi-account balances, transaction search and CSV export, file import (OFX, QIF, CAMT, CSV), auto-categorization rules, budgets and savings goals, asset tracking, net worth and income/expense reports, multi-currency FX conversion, a multi-user admin panel, TOTP two-factor authentication, OIDC login, and optional self-hosted AI agents with tool-use.
summary.cons: Bank sync via Enable Banking's free tier requires pre-linking accounts in the EB portal before connecting from Securo, or the connection returns no accounts; this suggests the free-tier path involves extra manual setup that first-time users could easily miss.
summary.fit: Given its Docker-based self-hosting model and AGPL-3.0 license, the project appears suited to individuals or teams willing to run their own infrastructure and who value data control; under AGPL terms, modifications used as a network service (SaaS) must also be released under AGPL-3.0.

repos.name: melgarafael / DeskcommCRM
repos.description: Open-source AI sales OS — self-hosted CRM with native AI agents + WhatsApp (WAHA). Open alternative to Kommo, Octadesk & Intercom for any business that sells by chat. MCP-ready, multi-tenant, LGPD.

summary.goal: DeskcommCRM is an open-source, self-hosted CRM described in the README as an AI-driven sales operating system for WhatsApp, combining AI agents that qualify leads and manage conversations with standard CRM features like kanban boards, contacts, and funnels. It is presented as an alternative to Kommo, Octadesk, and Intercom.
summary.usage: The documented path is to install on a VPS with Docker: clone the repository with `git clone https://github.com/melgarafael/DeskcommCRM.git`, then run `bash hostgator-setup-kit/install.sh`, which sets up the app, WhatsApp connection, and database. Later updates use `bash hostgator-setup-kit/update.sh`.
summary.pros: According to the README, the CRM includes AI agents that qualify leads and trigger follow-ups, configurable per-niche vocabulary (e.g., 'lead' becomes 'Client' or 'Patient'), a choice of AI provider (OpenRouter, Anthropic, or OpenAI), and no subscription fee since it runs under the MIT license on the operator's own server.
summary.cons: The README notes that Supabase's free-tier database does not perform backups automatically, so operators are expected to schedule the included `backup.sh` script themselves to avoid data loss between updates.
summary.fit: Because this is self-hosted software, it may fit users who are prepared to manage their own VPS, Supabase database, and AI provider keys, since the README describes support as community-based (GitHub Issues/Discussions) rather than guaranteed or SLA-backed.
